research_question: In neonates (≤28 days of age, term or preterm) with clinically or electrographically diagnosed seizures, what is the effect of phenobarbital versus levetiracetam as first-line anti-seizure medication on all-cause mortality before hospital discharge?
outcome_description: All-cause mortality before hospital discharge: the number of infants who died from any cause between randomisation and discharge from hospital (or death during the initial NICU/hospital admission), out of the number randomised (or, if not reported, the number analysed) in each arm. Only in-hospital/pre-discharge deaths are used; mortality reported at 3, 6, or 12 months or any post-discharge death is not used. Zero-event arms are recorded as 0 events with the arm denominator; studies that do not report deaths at all are excluded rather than imputed as zero. Arms are assigned by drug name from the group definitions (not table/figure column order), with phenobarbital always the treatment arm; for cross-over or add-on-after-failure designs, infants are counted in their originally randomised group; in multi-arm trials only the phenobarbital and levetiracetam arms are used.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR below 1 after signing, i.e. a positive effect size) means fewer deaths before hospital discharge with phenobarbital than with levetiracetam — favouring phenobarbital. Conversely, RR > 1 means more deaths with phenobarbital, favouring levetiracetam.
search_queries: phenobarbital versus levetiracetam neonatal seizures randomized trial
levetiracetam first-line treatment neonatal seizures controlled trial mortality
phenobarbitone anticonvulsant neonatal seizures trial outcome neonates
inclusion_criteria: Randomised or quasi-randomised trial enrolling neonates (up to 28 days of age, term or preterm) with clinically or electrographically diagnosed seizures
Compares phenobarbital (phenobarbitone) with levetiracetam as first-line anti-seizure medication in at least two of its arms (multi-arm trials eligible, using only these two arms)
Reports any quantitative data on deaths/mortality during the initial hospital or NICU stay (including explicit zero-event counts) from which a risk ratio can be computed
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, theoretical or protocol-only paper)
No comparison between a treatment and a control condition (single-arm or uncontrolled case series, observational cohorts without a comparator, non-randomised/non-quasi-randomised designs)
No usable quantitative outcome data for computing an effect size (no event counts/denominators, proportions, risk/odds ratios, or means+SDs reported for mortality)

Unrelated to the research topic: trials of seizure prophylaxis rather than treatment, trials in which neither arm is phenobarbital or levetiracetam, comparisons of the two drugs only as add-on/second-line therapy after failure of a first drug, non-neonatal populations, or mortality reported only after discharge (3/6/12-month follow-up)
moderators_to_extract: Gestational age category (term vs preterm vs mixed)
Primary seizure aetiology (e.g. hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy vs mixed)
Levetiracetam loading dose and phenobarbital loading dose
Randomisation type (randomised vs quasi-randomised) and blinding/risk of bias
Country/income setting and sample size category
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio with phenobarbital in the numerator and levetiracetam in the denominator, using in-hospital/pre-discharge all-cause death counts over the number randomised (or analysed if randomised numbers are unavailable). Expect sparse data and zero-event arms; use a method appropriate for rare events (e.g. Mantel-Haenszel without continuity correction where possible, retaining zero-event studies with their arm sizes). Do not pool seizure control, time to seizure cessation, EEG outcomes, adverse events, neurodevelopmental outcomes, or mechanical ventilation.
